title: Decision Receipt, version 3 (ZIFFER-SPEC-001 9.2, 8.6b AB-0..AB-6, 9.3)
description:
The SIGNED BODY of a Decision Receipt under receipt version 3, carried on leg F3.3 of the flow-leg register (ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 Annex A, Policy Engine -> Executor; the row read KMS -> Executor until ACP-110, and the KMS cannot be that sender: B-1a puts the canonical Proposal beside the receipt on this leg and the KMS never holds it, so the signed receipt returns to the Policy Engine on F3.2's response). The Executor trusts a signature, not a channel (9.1): B-4 forbids it accepting any instruction from any other source, so this object is the only thing in the system that can cause an external effect.

WHERE THE EDGE OF THIS OBJECT IS. Two clauses fix it. WE-2: the COSE payload is the canonical encoding of the receipt structure. AB-5: the bytes covered by the receipt signature are the canonical encoding of the receipt body WITHOUT the attestation entries. Every property below is inside the signature and nothing else is, which is also what makes AB-6 measurable -- the 4,096-byte bound is on THIS object's canonical encoding, and it is the whole reason version 3 exists.

WHAT IS NOT A FIELD, EACH ABSENT ON PURPOSE.
(1) The SIGNATURE. WE-1 makes COSE_Sign1 the carrier, so the signature is the envelope around this payload, never a member of it. The Python reference carries a sibling `sig` key and excludes it from the signed body by name (`SIGNED_EXCLUDE`), a stand-in for a COSE envelope it does not yet emit and which its own CRYPTO DISCLOSURE names as a gap. Giving `sig` a property here would make that stand-in look normative.
(2) The ATTESTATION ENTRIES. AB-1: the entries MUST travel alongside the receipt and MUST NOT appear in the signed body; they are bound solely by `attestation_digests` below. Note what the specification does not say -- it names no envelope structure, no field name and no ordering for that beside-channel. `attestations` is the reference implementation's choice of name, not the document's.
(3) `reversibility`. RV-2 is explicit: reversibility lives only in the signed bundle and there is 'no receipt field of record'. RV-3 recomputes it, because a receipt-asserted REVERSIBLE would suppress DR-9's acknowledgement exactly as v1.3.0's forged floor-only risk suppressed attestation (X1). The reference nevertheless reads a `reversibility` key when one is present; under this closed field set such a receipt is malformed, and that disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled.
(4) `attestation_id` and `action_id`. Both are DERIVED: the first is SHA-256 over the canonical Attestation Object (AT-1, AT-8a) and the Executor recomputes it (9.3 step 7b(v)); the second is the pair (proposal_hash, origin_nonce) pinned by the ledger (DS-6a, DS-6f). A transmitted identifier is a name for a binding, not evidence of one (RES-9), and a schema that gave either a property would invite exactly that read.

WHY THE FIELD SET IS CLOSED, AND THE CAVEAT THAT GOES WITH IT. `additionalProperties` is false and every property but `origin_nonce` is required. THE SPECIFICATION DOES NOT STATE THIS RULE. AT-8b closes the Attestation Object field set and calls the closure the security property itself; there is no AT-8b for the receipt. Closure is adopted here because it is the fail-safe direction -- an unknown key is refused rather than ignored, a missing key is refused rather than defaulted -- and because the alternative is a per-implementation field set on the one object whose canonical bytes are signed and whose size is capped. It is recorded as a gap, not presented as a reading: a clause saying for the receipt what AT-8b says for the object is a text change this schema cannot make.

Z4 DOES NOT REACH THIS OBJECT THE WAY IT REACHES THE ATTESTATION OBJECT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WORTH STATING RATHER THAN ASSUMED. An Attestation Object's ledger identity is a digest of itself, so two encodings are two ids and one human approval claims two slots (T-14). A receipt's ledger identity is `nonce`, a carried field consumed under CL-3, so two encodings of one receipt still claim one slot. What an optional field costs here is not amplification but DIVERGENCE: one verifier refuses the unknown key, another ignores it, and at the verifier a divergence is indistinguishable from a forgery. That is a weaker consequence than Z4's and it is still a reason to close the set.

ENCODING. Canonical CBOR, RFC 8949 section 4.2 (WE-1, WE-2) -- the same canonicalization AT-8a pins for the Attestation Object. JCS (RFC 8785) is the Proposal's rule and MUST NOT be used here. WE-3: a reference decoder emits JSON for review and JSON MUST NOT be accepted as receipt input, so the shape below is diagnostic form and never a wire form.

WHAT THIS SCHEMA CANNOT CONSTRAIN. Listed so that shape validity is never read as conformance; each item is a per-implementation obligation and several carry their own conformance case and mutant (AB-5).
- AB-2's ORDERING. `attestation_digests` MUST be sorted strictly ascending over the UTF-8 bytes of the digest strings including the `sha256:` prefix. JSON Schema has no sortedness keyword, so an unsorted list is shape-valid here and MUST still be refused under AB-2.
- AB-6's SIZE BOUND. 4,096 bytes of canonical encoding is a property of an encoding, not of a JSON shape, and AB-6 requires it be checked on measured bytes rather than on any proxy such as an entry count -- the first draft capped the count at 50 and measured 4,107 bytes at that cap.
- AB-4's CARDINALITY and AB-1's MEMBERSHIP. Both relate this object to entries that are not members of it, so neither is expressible here.
- L-14 / 9.3 step 5's WINDOW LENGTH: `expires_at - issued_at` <= 120 s is arithmetic across two fields.
- CR-3's conjunctive verification and CR-4's containment floor. `alg` names the suite; whether every declared primitive verified, and whether the suite contains every primitive the bundle floor names, are decided elsewhere and never from a transmitted value.
- WHETHER THIS IS A RE-DRIVE. DS-6b says a re-drive receipt MUST carry `origin_nonce`, and no field in the receipt declares that it is one, so the conditional obligation cannot be expressed at any layer that reads only this object.

SHARED TYPES ARE REFERENCED, NEVER REPEATED. `sha256` and `risk_level` come from attestation_object.schema.json, the 128-bit `b64:` nonce from ledger_claim.schema.json where CL-3 consumes it, and two come from the SIGNED BUNDLE root across the root boundary: `suite_id` from signature.schema.json, where CR-4's floor is registered, and `fidelity_class` from adapters.schema.json, the table TR-8 verifies this receipt's `fidelity` against (ACP-73; it lived in proposal.schema.json, on the side being verified, until that table existed). Each is defined once and pointed at from here. A second copy would be a second statement of one object, which is the defect this repository publishes corrections for -- and the generator halts on a duplicate `x-acp-name` within a root and across the two, so the copy would not even be silent. A `$ref` may cross roots for a named SCALAR only (ACP-78 M1): the vocabulary a receipt is compared against is owned by the signed side, and an object crossing would drag its field graph with it. This paragraph had said the opposite -- that a cross-root `$ref` was not a rule the generator had and `suite_id` was therefore one type in two files -- for the whole of M1, while the `alg` property below already crossed; prose describing a generator is exactly as trustworthy as prose describing anything else nothing executes.

That the homes of the wire-root types are scattered across message schemas is an accident of which file happened to need them first, not a design. The durable answer is one shared definitions file in this root that every message schema references; there is none, so the placement is recorded here rather than presented as intentional.

SUITE 12 CLASSIFICATION. At the schema layer every field is class T, because this document constrains SHAPE and shape is not authority. The Executor's obligations are elsewhere and are named on the individual properties rather than restated here: `proposal_hash` and the bundle basis are BOUND (9.3 steps 3 and 4), floor-only risk and fidelity are RECOMPUTED and the transmitted values only ever raise a critical alert on disagreement (TR-8, 9.3 step 7a), the operator identity is taken from the verified Attestation Objects and never from this body (Y4), and the origin nonce is read from the immutable ledger binding (DS-6f).

DISAGREEMENTS SURFACED BY WRITING THIS SCHEMA, PUBLISHED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED OVER. Section 9.2's example is the only enumeration of receipt fields the specification gives, and it omits two fields other clauses make mandatory: `alg` (CR-1 names the receipt explicitly, CR-5 makes it signature-covered) and `idempotency_key` (DS-6b: 'MUST be carried as a distinct receipt field'). An implementer building a receipt from that block alone emits one that is CR-1 non-conformant while conforming to the text they read, which is the PB-8 shape the document has already published a correction for. In the other direction, both current implementations omit nine fields the example carries -- `schema_id`, `schema_version`, `schema_hash`, `fidelity`, `context_snapshot_hash`, `rule_id`, `risk_level_effective`, `risk_level_floor_only` and `audit_id` -- and spell `issued_at` and `expires_at` as numeric epoch seconds where the example spells RFC 3339. Modelling the specification therefore makes every fixture in the repository invalid against this file. That is disclosed, not designed around; ACP-52 already records that nothing validates a fixture against these schemas and that the fixtures are schema-invalid.

receipt_version.description:
AB-0: exactly 3, verified BEFORE any other check, and every other value rejected including its absence. Written as an inclusive bound of exactly one value because that is what AB-0 admits.

THERE IS NO COMPATIBILITY WINDOW AND THE REASON IS NOT COMPATIBILITY. Version 2 is the weaker representation; a verifier that accepts both lets an attacker present version 2 and never face the digest binding at all. A transition window is therefore not a migration aid, it is a downgrade path -- the CR-4 shape one layer up, with the FORMAT rather than the suite negotiated by the party under verification.

The number is 3 and not 2 because section 9.2's published example already carried `"receipt_version": 2` for the containment form, and one version number with two meanings is the two-definitions defect at the wire.

A verifier MUST NOT let shape validation stand in for this check: a version-2 receipt has to be refused by the name AB-0, because the cross-language differential compares refusal names and a generic schema error is not one.

alg.description:
CR-1: every signed structure MUST carry an explicit `alg` naming a signature suite registered in the signed bundle, and the receipt is named in that clause. CR-5 makes it signature-covered, so an issuer cannot rewrite the suite without invalidating the receipt it travelled on.

Carrying the suite is not the same as choosing it. The FLOOR comes from the signed bundle and is satisfied by CONTAINMENT of primitives, never by rank (CR-4): a suite is a set, `hybrid-ed25519-mldsa65` and `slhdsa128s` are incomparable, and every implementation that built a rank table from the pre-v1.3.15 wording served a lattice signature to a deployment that had chosen hash-based precisely to avoid one. Reading the floor from anything transmitted asks the party under verification how strictly to judge it.

NOTE that section 9.2's receipt example does not show this field, while CR-1 and CR-5 require it. The clauses govern; the example is incomplete.

THE VALUE DOMAIN IS DECLARED ONCE, IN THE BUNDLE ROOT, and this field `$ref`s it across roots: `spec/schemas/bundle/signature.schema.json#/$defs/suite_id`. It was declared in both roots until ACP-78 M1 -- one vocabulary, two definitions, with each copy carrying its own note saying the two must move together, which is the arrangement that let the strict-Ed25519 rule sit in two languages. CR-4 compares the receipt's suite against the bundle's registered floor, so the two artifacts must draw from ONE set or the comparison is between two vocabularies that merely look alike. It is deliberately NOT `const`: listing only the hybrid suite would make a receipt signed under `ed25519` fail SHAPE validation when the required outcome is a CR-4 refusal naming the floor. A name outside the set is refused under CR-1 by the verifier and never defaulted to a known suite.

decision.description:
The graded outcome of section 8.4 step 11. 9.3 step 2: the Executor proceeds only on ALLOW.

DELIBERATELY NOT `const: "ALLOW"`, for the reason `suite_id` in the bundle signature schema is not a single-value enum: pinning the only acceptable value here would make a DENY receipt fail SHAPE validation when the required outcome is a refusal named 9.3-2. A check that fires under the wrong name is a divergence waiting to happen, because the cross-language differential compares names.

EO-1: HIGH is never auto-allowed by any configuration, so an ALLOW over a floor-HIGH action is a claim about a quorum, and that claim is checked against `attestation_digests` and the entries beside the receipt rather than believed.

proposal_hash.description:
The canonical Proposal this receipt authorises. 9.3 step 3: the Executor hashes the Proposal IT received over the same channel (B-1a), canonicalized identically, and compares -- it hashes what it will execute, never 'whatever the receipt describes'. Class B.

This field is a name for a binding. The binding is the comparison, and it exists because a receipt that merely asserts what it covers is a claim by the party under verification (RES-9).

schema_id.description:
SR-1: schemas are content-addressed by `schema_id` + `schema_version` + `schema_hash`, and SR-5 requires every Decision to carry the triple. The pattern is section 6.3's `AtomEnvelope`, so the receipt's identifier is the same type the ingress validated.

The triple is not decoration: TR-8 has the Executor verify `fidelity` against the bundle-registered adapter binding for THIS `schema_id`, so an unregistered id refuses rather than grading.

schema_version.description: Semver, per SR-1 and section 6.3's `AtomEnvelope`. Part of the content address, not a compatibility hint: SR-3 decides narrowing against a bounded lattice precisely because v1.2.0 left 'narrowing' undefined and a net-widening change could self-classify and bypass distinct-reviewer approval.

schema_hash.description: The third leg of the SR-1 content address. SR-2: the validator refuses to start on a signature or hash mismatch, so a receipt naming a schema hash the bundle does not carry describes a grammar nobody signed.

fidelity.description:
The adapter-stamped intent-fidelity class of the Proposal (SR-5). DIAGNOSTIC AND AUDIT ONLY, stated normatively in section 9.2's authority note.

9.3 step 7 has the Executor verify fidelity against the bundle-registered adapter binding for `schema_id`, and 7a makes disagreement with this transmitted value a CRITICAL ALERT rather than a preference: a validly-signed receipt asserting `F-HIGH` for a Proposal from an F-LOW-bound adapter means the signing substrate is emitting Decisions the bundle does not support (T-18).

TWO VALUES, NOT THREE, AND THE TYPE IS DEFINED ONCE. There is no `F-MEDIUM`: this class is what actually varied between the retired Door A / Door B binary, and it is a property of an INGRESS ADAPTER rather than a separate architecture; it is also orthogonal to the provider class (static entitlements against live directory sync), a conflation the document already carries a correction for in rows 7 and 8 of its applicability table. The type itself lives in the signed bundle's adapters.schema.json -- the table this value is verified AGAINST (ACP-73), where it was homed once that table existed; before that it lived in proposal.schema.json, on the side being verified -- and is referenced here rather than repeated: two definitions of one type is the defect this repository publishes corrections for, and the generator halts on a duplicate `x-acp-name` within a root and across the two.

policy_bundle_hash.description: The signed bundle the Decision was computed against. 9.3 step 4: it MUST match the bundle the Executor already trusts. Class B, and the direction matters -- the Executor compares against its own bundle rather than loading the one the receipt names, which would be the verifier taking its policy from the party under verification.

bundle_epoch.description:
Epoch of that bundle. 9.3 step 4 requires it to be at least the Executor's last-seen epoch, and the ledger records the high-water mark (CL-3), so a receipt naming an older epoch is a rollback attempt and fails closed.

Monotonicity is ALSO enforced one hop earlier, at the KMS, against a durable high-water mark before it will sign at all (9.1.1 step 5, RAD-3). Two enforcement points, neither redundant: the KMS check stops a stale-bundle Decision being minted, the Executor check stops one being replayed.

context_snapshot_hash.description:
The Context read the Decision was computed over (section 8.8 `snapshot_hash()`). Context reads are snapshot-consistent and AC-3 makes the consumed snapshot part of the audit record, so replay is exact rather than approximate.

Recording the snapshot does not make Context trustworthy, and the receipt is not where that is decided: TR-8 has the Executor recompute floor-only risk while IGNORING every Context-Store raise, which is why a compromised Context Store can still withhold a capability fact (DENY, safe) or raise a tier (more attestation, safe) but cannot suppress escalation.

rule_id.description:
The bundle rule that decided. AT-3 makes the rule identity part of what an attester is SHOWN -- floor tiers and the bundle `rule_id`s that raised the risk, deliberately not Context-asserted values, which is the separation that closes A-8's display path -- and section 9.2 carries one in the receipt for replay.

TWO CAVEATS, BOTH GAPS RATHER THAN DESIGN. No clause pins this identifier's syntax; the only pattern the specification attaches to a thing called `rule_id` belongs to a DIFFERENT object -- the firewall rule identifier inside section 6.3's `ModifyFirewallRule` payload, constrained to `^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$`, which the receipt example's own `RULE-002` would fail. One name, two normative meanings, which is the CL-7 shape the document has published a correction for. And AT-3 speaks of the rule idS that raised the risk, plural, while the receipt carries one; nothing says which one that is when several raised it. No pattern is asserted here because inventing one would be a third meaning.

risk_level_effective.description:
Risk after Context raises and accumulator effects (section 8.4 step 9, AC-4, RK-3 monotone max). DIAGNOSTIC AND AUDIT ONLY -- section 9.2's authority note is explicit that this field is NOT authoritative for any Executor control decision.

It is carried because replay needs it and refused authority because X1 was exactly this field's neighbour being believed. Effective risk can only ever be at or above floor-only risk, and the Executor keys every attestation requirement on the RECOMPUTED floor-only value (TR-8), so a receipt inflating this field buys an attacker nothing and deflating it changes nothing.

risk_level_floor_only.description:
Floor-only risk: the value derived from the target resource's signed tier floor and the bundle's risk functions, with every Context-Store raise ignored. DIAGNOSTIC AND AUDIT ONLY.

THIS IS THE FIELD RES-8 IS ABOUT. In v1.3.0 the Executor read it, and a forged `risk_level_floor_only` below the bundle-derived value suppressed the attestation requirement entirely (X1). TR-8 now has the Executor RECOMPUTE it from the trusted bundle's floors and risk functions applied to the independently-received canonical Proposal, and 9.3 step 7a makes disagreement with the value transmitted here a CRITICAL ALERT, not a log line: it means the signing substrate produced a Decision the bundle does not support (T-18).

The fail-safe defaults that feed the recomputation live in the bundle schemas and are not restated here: a resource absent from `floors.json` is T3 (RK-1), an action with no risk function is REFUSED at 8.4-3 rather than graded HIGH, and unknown is never LOW (P-4).

attestation_digests.description:
AB-1: the receipt's commitment to the attestations, one digest per entry, with the entries themselves travelling alongside and never inside the signed body. THIS ARRAY IS THE ENTIRE BINDING under version 3.

THE PREIMAGE IS THE WHOLE ENTRY, AND THAT IS THE TRAP. Each digest is `sha256:` over the canonical encoding of the complete entry -- `obj`, `kind`, `attester` and `sig` together -- and MUST NOT be `attestation_id`, nor any digest whose preimage is the Attestation Object alone. `attestation_id` already exists, is already normative, and is the obvious thing to reuse; it is wrong. The AT-1 field set is closed over the OBJECT and contains no `kind`, no `attester` and no `sig`, while quorum composition is decided from the ENTRY -- `kind` selects approval or confirmation, `attester` supplies the identity distinctness is counted over -- and the attester signs neither. Under version 2 containment sealed them. Commit only to the object and an attacker on the transport path flips one entry's `kind` from `confirmation` to `approval` while every digest still matches. Two identifiers now exist and MUST NOT be merged: `attestation_id` is what the ledger consumes for single use under CL-3, this digest is what the receipt authorised byte for byte.

WHAT `uniqueItems` DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. AB-3 forbids repeated digests and requires the check at THIS layer rather than delegated to CL-3's `attestation_id` claim, because CL-3 is object-scoped and needs a Consumption Ledger -- a stateless verifier has no ledger for it to fire in, and there AB-3 is the only defence. `uniqueItems` is the shape statement of that rule; a duplicate MUST still be refused under the name AB-3, not as a generic validation error. In an Executor that does hold a ledger AB-3 is masked by CL-3 and kills no mutant, which is recorded as a positive-path obligation rather than dressed up as a control.

AN EMPTY ARRAY IS VALID AND `minItems` IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. A LOW or MEDIUM Decision carries no attestations. Requiring one entry would make every fast-path receipt malformed, and requiring the quorum size here would be reading the size of the quorum off the receipt -- AB-4 says quorum MUST be counted from VERIFIED attestations and never derived from the length of this list, which is AT-3's defect one layer down.

ORDERING IS NOT CONSTRAINED HERE AND IS NORMATIVE: AB-2 requires strictly ascending lexicographic order over the UTF-8 bytes of the digest strings INCLUDING the `sha256:` prefix, because without a declared order one quorum yields two canonical encodings of one receipt and therefore two receipt identities -- the Z4 encoding split reached with no optional field involved.

tenant_id.description:
The tenant the Decision was made for. 9.3 step 8: it MUST equal the tenant of the independently-received Proposal, so a validly-signed receipt from another tenant fails closed rather than executing across the boundary.

The ledger is shared per tenant and its uniqueness constraints are keyed on `(tenant_id, artifact_class, identifier)` (CL-5), so this value also decides which single-use registry a nonce is claimed in. No pattern is pinned because the specification pins none.

operator.description:
The operator the action is attributed to. DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, and this is stated normatively rather than as guidance (section 9.2's authority note, Y4).

The authoritative operator identity for approver-distinctness (AT-2) and for the 9.3 step 9 capability recheck is `obj.operator` inside each verified Attestation Object, which is signature-covered; 9.3 step 7b(iii-a) requires it to be identical across every entry and requires the identity to be taken from the verified object, NEVER resolved in favour of this body field. A receipt whose body `operator` differs from the attested one fails closed. Mechanized as `Y4_OperatorTamperDetected`.

Below floor-HIGH no quorum exists and there is no attested operator to prefer, so this field is what audit records -- which is a disclosed asymmetry, not a second authority.

issued_at.description:
RFC 3339 instant of issuance, as section 9.2 renders it. 9.3 step 5: not future beyond a 5 s skew allowance.

Evaluated against NTS-disciplined wall time within the L-20 skew allowance, never against a monotonic clock -- the two are different quantities and DP-52 states the distinction; leg F9.1 carries the dependency.

TWO DISAGREEMENTS ARE RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN RESOLVED. Both current implementations spell this field as numeric epoch seconds, because 9.3 step 5 does arithmetic on it, while the specification renders it RFC 3339 in the only place it shows a receipt; the schema follows the specification. And RFC 3339 admits several spellings of one instant -- `Z` against `+00:00`, fractional seconds present or absent -- so a canonical-CBOR body containing one is not yet one encoding per instant. For the receipt that costs a diagnostic mismatch; for the Attestation Object, whose id is a digest of itself, it is Z4's two-ids consequence reached through a type no clause pins, which is the WE-4 shape one layer over.

expires_at.description:
RFC 3339 instant after which the receipt is void. 9.3 step 5 refuses an expired receipt AND enforces `expires_at - issued_at <= 120 s`.

THE WINDOW LENGTH IS EXECUTOR-ENFORCED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF Y2. Both endpoints are written by the KMS, so a verifier that only checks 'not yet expired' has delegated the validity window to the party under verification: a compromised signer issues a receipt valid for a week and every subsequent check still passes. Violation fails closed with a critical alert.

The relation between the two fields cannot be expressed in this schema, so shape validity says nothing about it (DR-6 depends on the same bound: a hold window at or above the L-14 ceiling would outlive receipt validity and fails closed).

nonce.description:
The receipt nonce, claimed atomically against the Consumption Ledger at 9.3 step 6 (CL-2 compare-and-swap; if the ledger is unavailable the Executor fails closed; CL-4 keeps the claim for at least receipt validity plus 24 h, because a registry that forgets a nonce before the receipt expires is a replay window). Single use is enforced by that claim, not asserted as a property.

IT IS ALSO THE ORIGIN OF ACTION IDENTITY. DS-6a: the nonce of the FIRST receipt issued for a Proposal becomes `origin_nonce`, and DS-6f has the ledger claim the immutable `proposal_hash -> origin_nonce` binding atomically with this claim. That binding is written once and read many times, a rebind attempt is a critical alert, and its retention is indefinite because an expiring origin binding reopens Z3 for any long-lived re-drive.

CHECKED AT 9.3 STEP 6, BEFORE THE CLAIM, IN BOTH LANGUAGES (ACP-89 -- this paragraph recorded a gap until then, and the gap is why it is still here). WE-4 governs this field exactly as it governs the attestation nonce -- the `b64:` prefix is part of the value, carried and hashed as that string -- and for three releases nothing read the clause here: the value went straight into the ledger claim in the reference and was unread in `acp-decision`, so two spellings of one nonce claimed two ledger slots, which is T-13 through the hole WE-4 exists to close. Step 6 now reads the nonce BEFORE it claims: a value that is not `b64:` + RFC 4648 section 4 with padding refuses under WE-4, a well-formed value that is not 128-bit then refuses under L-17, and only the validated string reaches the ledger -- so a malformed nonce never consumes a slot, and it is rejected rather than normalized for the reason the next paragraph gives. `reference/src/acp_executor.py` and `crates/acp-decision/src/decide.rs` carry the two checks at the same position in the same order, and the cross-language differential compares both refusal NAMES rather than both verdicts. WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT REACH, because a control that overstates itself here is the defect this paragraph was written about: only the stateless half is checked -- the CL-2 claim and L-17's retention half (CL-4) are the ledger's and are absent from `acp-decision` (ACP-46) -- and nothing validates a receipt against this schema at any point (ACP-52), so the pattern below is enforced by two implementations that agree with it, never by a validator reading this file.

THE TYPE IS DEFINED ONCE AND THE PATTERN IS TWO RULES THAT REFUSE UNDER DIFFERENT NAMES. `b64:` followed by the RFC 4648 section 4 alphabet WITH padding is WE-4, the wire type; the twenty-two characters plus `==` are L-17's 128 bits. A verifier folding them into one check answers WE-4 for a 64-bit nonce, which is a perfectly well-formed `b64:` value -- the wrong clause name, and the cross-language differential compares names. The prefix is PART OF THE VALUE: WE-4 requires it be carried, hashed and signed as that string, and stripping it, dropping the padding or substituting the URL-safe alphabet each produce a DIFFERENT value that MUST be rejected rather than normalized -- normalizing makes one verifier accept both spellings and hands the divergence to the next implementation, where it is indistinguishable from a forgery. The type was pinned at the root only in v1.3.18, after existing solely inside section 9.2's diagnostic JSON with no clause saying whether the prefix counted; it was found by writing a schema (ACP-87), which is the argument for writing them. It is referenced from ledger_claim.schema.json rather than repeated here, because the ledger is where a nonce is consumed and one wire type must have one definition.

audit_id.description:
The identifier of the audit record for this Decision, carried so a receipt can be tied to the hash-chained audit entry (AU-1) without a search. Section 9.2 carries it; R-1 uses the same name for the identifier returned with a rejection, so one value class spans both outcomes.

NO CLAUSE PINS ITS SYNTAX, and none is invented here -- `minLength`/`maxLength` bound the shape and nothing more. Note also what this field is NOT: a receipt naming an audit id is not evidence that the record exists or that the chain contains it. AU-3a's detection rests on multi-party anchoring of the chain, never on an identifier the same party transmits.

idempotency_key.description:
The target idempotency key, `SHA-256(canonical(action_id))` where `action_id` is the pair `(proposal_hash, origin_nonce)`. DS-6b requires it be carried as a distinct receipt field; DS-1 requires the Executor use it as the target's idempotency key, which is what makes exactly-once hold ACROSS re-drives.

ACTION IDENTITY IS NOT AUTHORIZATION IDENTITY, AND CONFLATING THEM WAS Y3. Through v1.3.3 this key was `attestation_id`, which is fresh on every re-drive -- so in exactly the lost-outcome case DS-3 exists to handle, the target saw a new key for an action that may already have committed and a floor-HIGH non-idempotent action doubled. DS-6c keeps both properties: the key is stable, the authorization is fresh.

IT IS TRANSMITTED AND IT IS NOT BELIEVED. The Executor derives the key from the ledger-pinned origin binding and compares (DS-6f); a re-drive receipt whose key differs from the ledger-derived value fails closed. DS-6d forbids a coarser key such as `proposal_hash` alone, which would suppress a legitimate second execution of an identical Proposal.

Section 9.2's example does not show this field although DS-6b says it MUST be carried, and the reference treats it as optional; both are recorded as gaps.

origin_nonce.description:
THE ONE OPTIONAL FIELD IN THIS SCHEMA, and the justification is owed rather than assumed.

WHAT IT IS. The receipt nonce of the FIRST receipt issued for this Proposal (DS-6a). DS-6b requires a re-drive receipt to carry it. DS-6f then makes the carried value DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: the Executor reads `origin_nonce` from the immutable ledger binding and derives `idempotency_key` from the value it read, and if this field is present it MUST equal the ledger value or the Executor fails closed with a critical alert.

WHY IT IS OPTIONAL RATHER THAN REQUIRED. DS-6f says 'if present', in those words, so requiring it would contradict the text; and a first receipt has no origin other than its own nonce, so there is nothing for it to carry. The alternative -- omitting the property entirely -- is worse under `additionalProperties: false`, because it would make every conformant re-drive receipt malformed.

WHY THAT IS NOT Z4 HERE, STATED SO THE EXEMPTION IS ARGUED RATHER THAN CLAIMED. Z4's consequence is two canonical encodings of one object yielding two ids and therefore two ledger slots. That reaches the Attestation Object because its ledger identity IS a digest of itself. A receipt's ledger identity is `nonce`, carried, so present-and-absent forms of one receipt still claim one slot. And omission cannot move the idempotency key, because DS-6f makes the ledger the source and this field merely a cross-check against it -- which is exactly the fix for Z3, where DS-6b as first drafted required only that the claimed origin be A consumed nonce. That is a MEMBERSHIP test, not a PINNING test: a compromised KMS named any other consumed nonce, the key moved, the target could not deduplicate, and the floor-HIGH action doubled. Fourth recurrence of the RES-8 class, in the machinery the previous fix introduced.

WHAT OMITTING IT DOES COST: the diagnostic cross-check disappears, so a signing substrate that has lost track of an origin binding produces a receipt nobody can tell apart from a correct one until the ledger is consulted. The field set is therefore NOT closed, and the specification has no way to say 'this is a re-drive' that would let the obligation be expressed conditionally. Recorded as a gap.

Same 128-bit `b64:` wire type as `nonce`, referenced from its single definition; the WE-4 and L-17 rules written out on that field apply here unchanged.

decision_outcome.description:
The three outcomes of the section 8.4 grading fold: ALLOW executes, ATTEST routes to a human quorum, DENY refuses.

NOT ORDERED. These are outcomes, not a severity scale, and a derived comparison over them would invite `>= ALLOW`-shaped code that has no meaning. P-4 makes DENY the default for no matching rule, unknown capability, unclassified resource or unavailable Context Store, each with its own reason code -- so DENY is where the fold lands when it knows nothing, not the far end of a ranking.

EO-1: HIGH MUST NOT be auto-allowed by any configuration; there is no flag that makes step 11 emit ALLOW for HIGH.
